title: GPU Fleet Allocator — Concept V2: Wireframes & Grooming Notes
content:
Purpose and audience:
This doc captures a second‑iteration concept for the Dedicated Capacity management UI we’re calling GPU Fleet Allocator. Audience: infra/product PMs, console frontend, SREs and ML platform engineers who will operate/purchase dedicated pools.

Why another variant (v2):
- Feedback from initial pool reservation sketches showed confusion around burst vs reserved capacity semantics.
- Need clearer cost preview prior to committing reservations.
- Want to combine live metrics with reservation calendar to make tradeoffs visible.

High level goals:
- Reduce cognitive load when creating/managing pools and reservations (single page summary + guided modal flows).
- Surface autoscaling rules and their cost/latency impact before save.
- Make bursts explicit (capacity type, duration, preemption rules).
- Provide quick remediation actions (re-route, fallback model, scale-down) from the pool detail view.

Primary personas and jobs-to-be-done:
- ML Platform Engineer: create pool, pin models, set SLA targets, and write autoscaling rules. Wants predictable throughput and ability to reserve capacity for critical jobs.
- Infra SRE: monitor pool health, emergency drain, increase/decrease allowed bursts. Wants fast access to logs, traces, and rollback.
- Product PM/Finance partner: preview cost impact for reservations and understand utilization. Wants exportable cost estimates.

Top-level pages (wireframe map):
1) Pools list (landing): compact table with columns: pool name, region, GPU type, reserved v. available capacity, current utilization (sparkline), next reservation start, health badge. Actions: Open, Reserve, Scale. Secondary: filter by region/gpu-type/tag.
2) Pool detail (single-column center): header with status, active reservations, health. Tabs: Metrics (latency, throughput, token/s), Reservations (calendar heatmap), Autoscaling rules (visual rule builder), Allocation (model pinning & fallbacks), Audit & Logs. Persistent right rail: cost estimate + quick actions (force-scale, emergency-drain, open support).
3) Reservation modal (guided): step 1 choose capacity: fixed reservation vs flexible reservation (committed hours per month) vs burst-only; step 2 choose shape: GPU count, memory class, node affinity; step 3 schedule: one-off, recurring, recurring with blackout dates; step 4 policies: preemption allowed?, automatic fallback?; step 5 preview: estimated monthly charge, estimated SLO headroom, utilization delta, warnings.

Wireframe notes (visual language):
- Use a 3-column layout inside pool detail for dense info: main canvas (metrics & calendar), left compact nav for tab anchors, right rail for cost/actions.
- Calendar: weekly heatmap with stacked bars showing reserved vs on-demand vs burst usage. Hover reveals reservation owner, start/end, expected cost.
- Autoscaling rule builder: drag‑to‑reorder rules. Each rule card shows trigger (cpu/queue/latency), action (scale up N GPUs, add burst allowance), cooldown, and estimated cost impact. Inline chalkboard microcopy: "Impact: ~+12% monthly cost, median tail latency -120ms".
- Reservations list: exposed in a table with icons for recurring, conflict, and preemption enabled. Bulk actions: cancel, edit recurrence, transfer ownership.

Interaction and microcopy examples:
- Reserve button microcopy: "Reserve capacity" (primary) and "Try burst (pay-as-you-go)" (secondary).
- Burst modal header: "Temporary burst — non‑committed GPUs"; body: "Bursts are best for traffic spikes; may be preempted and will incur on-demand rates. Add a fallback policy to avoid errors."
- Autoscale rule hint: "Use queue length for batch jobs, latency for interactive models."
- Error state when over-quota: "You don’t have quota for requested GPU type in this region. Request quota increase or choose an alternate GPU."

Edge cases & constraints:
- Overlapping reservations in same zone: warn and show conflict resolution suggestions (shift reservation, reduce GPU count, propose alternate zone with cost diff).
- Preemptable bursts: must label as "best effort" in calendar and provide explicit fallback routing options (e.g., route to smaller model or hosted API).
- Interplay with Dedicated SLA: reservations that reduce available capacity for higher-priority customers should require an approval workflow.

Accessibility & internationalization:
- Keyboard-first flows for reservation modal (tab order consistent, Enter confirms primary action).
- Provide high contrast color options for heatmap and badges; avoid red/green-only semantics.
- All dates shown with timezone context; default to pool region timezone but allow team override.

Metrics to show on pool detail page:
- 1m/5m/15m token throughput, avg latency P50/P95, queued requests, GPU utilization %, average KV cache hit rate.
- Cost metrics: estimated $/hour and $/month for current configuration, delta vs. baseline, amortized cost per 1M tokens.

Backlog grooming (priority + estimate):
- INF-1423 Create Pools list page skeleton (2 devs, 3 sprint points) - High
- UX-398 Reservation modal v2 flow + copy (design 3 days, dev 2 sprint points) - High
- INF-1499 Calendar heatmap + hover details (data infra needed) (5 points) - Medium
- INF-1508 Autoscale rule builder (drag reorder + preview) (8 points) - High
- INF-1514 Burst accounting integration with billing (requires billing API) (5 points) - High
- INF-1532 Approval workflow for large reservations (>X GPUs or >$Y) (3 points) - Medium
- INF-1540 Accessibility keyboard flows & QA (2 points) - High

Design decisions needed (open questions):
- Pricing preview: should it show list price vs commitment discount? (PM/Finance decision)
- Approval threshold: propose $5k/month or 50 GPUs — what is the org policy? (Ops + Sales input)
- Autoscale rollback behavior: should there be an automatic rollback on error or a manual action only?

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: users confuse burst with reserved capacity -> mitigate with required modal confirmation and inline examples.
- Risk: inaccurate cost previews cause downstream billing disputes -> mitigation: show clear disclaimers and link to billing breakdown; require acceptance for large reservations.
- Risk: calendar complexity -> provide a compact condensed view and an advanced toggle.

Acceptance criteria (for MVP):
- Pools list shows accurate reserved/available capacity and links to pool detail.
- Reservation modal supports one-off and recurring reservations with cost preview.
- Autoscaling rules can be created with at least 3 trigger types and show previewed cost impact.
- Burst request flow clearly indicates preemption and fallback options.
- Basic audit trail entries for reservations and scaling actions visible in Pool detail.

Testing & rollout plan:
- Internal alpha with 3 platform teams for 2 sprints; collect qualitative feedback and instrument NPS-style question post-flow.
- Beta release to 10% of traffic for dedicated customers with opt-in reservations. Monitor refunds/charge disputes during first 30 days.

Next steps (owner assignments):
- Maya: finalize annotated wireframes (Deliverables: Figma file + clickable prototype) — due 2025-03-07.
- Evan: spike for heatmap data model and API contracts (Deliverable: API spec + perf budget) — due 2025-02-21.
- Diego: coordinate billing hook for cost preview (Deliverable: billing API integration plan) — due 2025-03-01.
- Priya: draft copy for modals and error states; handoff to localization — due 2025-02-20.

Appendix: quick sketch palette and components (text):
- Header badges: green=healthy, amber=degraded, red=down, gray=unknown.
- Small components: reservation-pill (color by type), quick-action-menu (three dots), cost-chip (dollar + tooltip).

Reference links and inspiration:
- Kubernetes cluster autoscaler UIs, Databricks reserved instance console, AWS Savings Plans UX notes (linked in Confluence).

Notes: this doc intentionally focuses on operational clarity and cost transparency. The goal is to reduce the time-to-decision for ops teams when buying or adjusting capacity and make it difficult to accidentally spend on bursts without an explicit fallback policy.

Feedback requested from reviewers:
- Is the calendar heatmap the right primary visualization for reservations? Alternatives: gantt timeline or stacked day view.
- Approval threshold recommendations and required approval fields.
- Any compliance/security blockers for showing tenant-level cost estimates in the console.

End of doc.
